newsitem.title: INDIA: Bomb explodes ahead of Indian PM Gujral's arrival.
newsitem.headline: Bomb explodes ahead of Indian PM Gujral's arrival.

text.p: A powerful bomb exploded on Thursday near an airport in northeast India where Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral was due to land hours later, police officials said.
They said the blast occurred about two km (1.5 mile) from Imphal airport at about 12:30 p.m. -- less than five hours before Gujral's arrival during a five-day tour of the insurgency-torn northeast.
No casualties were reported. Police said they suspected a separatist guerrilla group had planted the bomb.
Tribal insurgents killed 11 paramilitary soldiers in an ambush on Wednesday in Manipur, the state which has Imphal as its capital.

The northeast is linked to the rest of India only by a narrow strip of land passing north of Bangladesh. Five of the seven states, Manipur, Nagaland, Assam, Tripura and Mizoram, have been hit by insurgency movements.
On his arrival in Imphal, the prime minister urged the people of Manipur to help the government bring peace to the region.
"Forget the past," Gujral told a public meeting. "The time has come for all of us to say goodbye to guns. Join us in this effort to bring in an era of peace for development."
Gujral arrived in Imphal from Agartala, capital of the state of Tripura, He visited Guwahati, the capital of Assam, on Monday and was greeted by a general strike.
Gujral said he expected India's proposal for transit through Bangladesh would lead to economic development of the neglected region and help end the insurgencies.

Gujral said the government was ready to hold unconditional talks with insurgents within the framework of the Indian constitution, adding that his centre-left government was committed to solving the region's problems.
"Everything can be solved through negotiations. The United Front government is approaching the problems of the northeast with a view to achieving a breakthrough," he said.
